limitations_and_boundaries: Memory requirement grows linearly with dataset size in full-batch gradient descent.
Framework does not naturally support edge features and is limited to undirected graphs.
Implicit assumptions of locality and equal importance of self-connections vs. neighboring edges.
Mini-batch stochastic gradient descent may be needed for very large and densely connected graphs.
Directed edges and edge features can be handled by representing the original directed graph as an undirected bipartite graph with additional nodes.

research_questions.statement: Can a scalable graph convolutional network approach improve semi-supervised node classification on graph-structured data?

provenance.text_excerpt: Propagation of feature information from neighboring nodes in every layer improves classification performance in comparison to methods like ICA (Lu & Getoor, 2003), where only label information is aggregated.

methods.name: Graph Convolutional Network (GCN)
methods.protocol_description: Two-layer GCN with layer-wise propagation rule based on first-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions. Trained with Adam (lr=0.01), early stopping (window 10), Glorot initialization, row-normalized input features. Hyperparameters (dropout, L2 reg, hidden units) optimized on Cora validation set (500 labeled nodes). Max 200 epochs. For random graphs: 32 hidden units, no regularization.

methods.name: Iterative Classification Algorithm (ICA)
methods.protocol_description: ICA with two logistic regression classifiers (local and relational). Local classifier bootstraps labels; relational classifier runs 10 iterations. L2 reg and aggregation operator chosen per dataset via validation set.

methods.protocol_description: Best-performing model variant (transductive vs. inductive) from Yang et al. (2016).
